Research

CoMET

Condition-Based Monitoring of Execution with Behaviour Trees for Failure Detection in Robotic Manipulation

Code on GitHub

CoMET turns a manipulation task into a behaviour tree with explicit conditions. In the basketball task, for example, the ball should still be in the gripper on the way to the hoop. CoMET checks camera views at waypoints and monitors robot signals between them to identify when a condition stops holding.

Demo

How AHA fits into the evaluation

I use FailGen from the AHA project to introduce failures into RLBench demonstrations. This lets me compare a successful run with one in which the robot misses a grasp or drops an object. The video compares CoMET with AHA-based baselines across 78 manipulation tasks.
